page: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system includes 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. It is equipped with 1890 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any GPU accelerators. The CPU architecture is x86_64, featuring a massive 480 MB L3 cache and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions.

In benchmark evaluations, the D32ds_v7 demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2232.0 and single-threaded gzip compression throughput of 36.5 GB/sec. Multi-threaded decompression is also strong, with bzip3 reaching 231.56 GB/sec. Its memory subsystem delivers a read-only cached small-block bandwidth of 2684.62 GB/sec, while large-block uncached read and write speeds reach 166.74 GB/sec and 65.26 GB/sec respectively. For AI workloads, the hardware-assisted AMX instructions enable strong CPU-based LLM inference, processing 3133.77 tokens/sec for a small 135M model and 219.58 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model.

From a cost efficiency perspective, the D32ds_v7 offers a balanced resource density, combining high-frequency dedicated Intel compute with a substantial local storage allocation. This eliminates the immediate need for external storage attachments for disk-heavy operations, optimizing the overall resource-to-cost profile. The server is highly suited for workloads such as relational databases, static web serving, text and image processing, and intermediate-scale CPU-based machine learning inference.
